subject: Retroactive SLA concession request — account stabilization
messages:
From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@optiserve.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@optiserve.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Unplanned latency on Nov 9 — request for retroactive SLA adjustment

Hi Jonas,

We experienced elevated tail latency from Redwood on Nov 9 between 03:12–04:40 UTC that materially affected our billing and batch ingest pipelines. Our SREs traced the burst to model-variant routing and sustained p50/p95 degradation for ~90 minutes. Impact: delays to overnight reconciliation jobs and 17% higher compute for retries.

We appreciate the support from the ops team during the window. Given the disruption, OptiServe is requesting a retroactive adjustment to our November invoice: specifically, a one-month service credit OR a bespoke credit equivalent to 25% of the November invoice plus two weeks of complimentary service. We are open to either option but would like confirmation from Redwood leadership and an estimated timeline for approval.

Please advise next steps — legal review, finance sign-off, or exec approval needed? We are aiming to finalize our month-end reconciliation on Nov 30.

Thanks,
Samantha Green
Head of Platform Reliability
OptiServe

Attachments: incident-summary-optiserve-nov9.pdf (customer attachment)

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@optiserve.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unplanned latency on Nov 9 — request for retroactive SLA adjustment

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear summary and for sending over the incident timeline. Really sorry this disrupted your flows.

Internally I'm escalating this for an executive concession review. My initial read: OptiServe is a mid-tier committed account (monthly commit ~ $48k) and the outage window looks like a significant degradation against our documented SLO. Per standard practice, we can propose either:

- Option A (simple): one pro-rated month credit (equivalent to one month of committed spend).
- Option B (custom): 25% credit on the November invoice + account credit covering 14 days of service (applied as a negative line on next invoice).

I'll route this to finance and legal for quick review and loop in Karthik / Marissa for exec sign-off. Can you confirm whether OptiServe prefers Option A or Option B? If you want Option B, please confirm the November invoice amount (or I can pull it from our billing system if you prefer).

Next steps: I'll request an expedited concession approval and aim to have a decision within 48–72 hours.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Unplanned latency on Nov 9 — request for retroactive SLA adjustment

Jonas — thanks for pulling this together. Quick internal read from GTM + finance:

- OptiServe is strategic (we've seen ~12% QoQ growth). We should aim to preserve the relationship while keeping precedent limited.
- Legal will require a short closure agreement (customer ack of remediation + acceptance of credit) for our records.
- Finance prefers a structured credit vs a blanket free month to reduce churn risk.

Proposed concession for exec approval: a capped hybrid that we can present to the customer as a single figure, keeps precedent tight:

1) 20% credit on November invoice (one-off, applied to Dec billing)
2) + 10 service-credit days applied to their account (not an extra month)
3) Require customer to sign a short closure statement confirming acceptance and that no further claims will be raised for this incident window.

I attached a draft "proposed-credit-schedule.xlsx" and a short "closure-agreement.docx" for legal to quick-check. If Karthik is comfortable, we can approve as an exec one-off with the condition that legal and finance sign the paperwork.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed-credit-schedule.xlsx; closure-agreement.docx

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unplanned latency on Nov 9 — request for retroactive SLA adjustment

Thanks — reviewed the draft. I support a constrained concession that balances customer goodwill and precedent control. My notes:

- Approve: 20% credit on November invoice + 10 service-credit days (applied as account credit).
- Condition: Customer must sign the closure statement and accept that remedy in-lieu of other financial claims.
- Also ask Legal to add a non-precedent clause: "This concession is made on a one-time, non-precedential basis and does not alter the written SLA."

Finance: please confirm the accounting treatment (one-off contra vs recurring credit). Naomi — can you confirm and loop legal for final wording?

Once legal signs off, Jonas please confirm to Samantha with the proposed offer and attach the closure agreement + credit schedule. Aim for a DocuSign by EOD Nov 23 if possible.

Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Final offer: one-time credit + service days (requires signed closure agreement)

Hi Samantha — thank you for your patience. After internal review with Sales Ops, Finance, and Legal we can offer the following one-time concession for the Nov 9 latency window: 

1) A one-off 20% credit on the November invoice (credit amount = $9,600).
2) Ten (10) service-credit days applied to your account, valid for 90 days.
3) Closure agreement to be signed via DocuSign acknowledging acceptance of the remedy and confirming no further claims for this incident. The agreement includes a non-precedent clause.

Attachments: updated proposed-credit-schedule.xlsx; closure-agreement.docx
DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/OPTI-CLOSE-123

If this is acceptable, please sign the closure agreement and we'll apply the credit to your December invoice and load the service days to your account within 3 business days of signature. If you prefer the alternate offer (one month pro-rated free month) let me know and I'll escalate further but we prefer the structured credit above to preserve consistent accounting treatment.

Appreciate you working with us on this — we're committed to restoring confidence and will follow up with a post-incident remediation note once Ops completes the full RCA.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
